title: SLO blueprints and dynamic error-budget borrowing for multi-region model endpoints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Define a concise set of SLO blueprints and an operational policy that enables safe, automated borrowing and repayment of error budget across model endpoints and regions. This ticket formalizes: (1) canonical SLI definitions for model endpoints (latency, success, quality), (2) three SLO templates (expedited, standard, best-effort) with example thresholds and error-budget windows, (3) a dynamic error-budget-borrowing algorithm to temporarily prioritize critical endpoints/regions, (4) circuit-breaker choreography and progressive load-shedding thresholds tied to SLO state, and (5) observability+runbook artifacts needed for on-call and automation. This is targeted at hosted and dedicated model endpoints and covers cross-region failover behavior when regional capacity shortfalls occur.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI definitions published in the engineering reliability docs and reviewed by at least 2 on-call engineers and 1 PM
Three SLO templates (Expedited/Standard/Best-effort) published with numerical examples and recommended use-cases
Automated borrowing policy documented: conditions to borrow, maximum borrow window, repayment policy, and priority ordering for endpoints/clients
Circuit breaker thresholds and progressive load-shedding steps defined and validated in a synthetic load test against a staging fleet
Dashboards (per-endpoint SLI, error-budget burn-rate, regional headroom) and 3 alert rules created in Grafana/Observability and linked in the ticket
Runbook describing operator actions for cross-region failover, emergency rollback, and post-incident reconciliation included
implementation_steps: Draft SLI measurement spec for success rate, latency quantiles (P50/P95/P99), and quality SLI (eval-based OKR)
Design SLO templates and example windows (30d/7d/1d) and draft error-budget arithmetic
Design borrowing algorithm: eligibility, priority ranking, max borrowed % of budget, repayment schedule
Define circuit breaker states (Closed, Throttling, Open) and their triggers (burn-rate, backend error spike, regional capacity loss)
Wire telemetry: add per-endpoint tagging for model, route, region; ensure logs include decision reason for any throttle/failover
Create dashboards and alerts; instrument synthetic canary jobs to validate policy under constrained capacity
Run tabletop exercises with SREs and PMs to validate runbook language and on-call actions
Implement automation glue in routing layer to apply priority throttles and trigger regional failover based on policy
metrics_and_sli_defs: success_rate: ratio of responses with 2xx/stream-complete events to total requests in 1m windows (exclude client-aborts and authenticated 4xx where request is malformed)
latency_ms: server-side generation latency measured from request accept to first token emitted and to completion; report P50/P95/P99 over 5m and 1h windows
quality_sli: periodic evaluation using a small curated prompt set (daily) comparing model outputs to golden labels; quality_sli expressed as percent passing quality gate
error_budget: 1 - SLO_target over the configured window. Burn rate = error_rate / (1 - SLO_target) normalized to budget window
headroom_score: region_capacity_remaining / estimated_peak_demand (0-1); used by routing policy to decide spillover
dashboards_and_alerts: Per-endpoint SLO overview: SLI charts, error-budget remaining (30d/7d/1d), burn-rate heatmap
Regional headroom board: capacity, active queues, headroom_score, failover events
Alert: headroom_score < 0.25 in a region for > 5m (P1)
Alert: circuit-breaker state changed to Throttling/Open for any endpoint (P0)
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish SLI/SLO specs, SRE review, and finalize numeric templates
Week 2: Implement telemetry tags and dashboards; synthetic canaries to validate metric correctness
Week 3: Deploy controller in staging that enforces borrowing+throttling policy behind a feature flag; run load tests
Week 4: Enable in production for a small set of non-critical endpoints (best-effort template) and monitor for 72h
Week 5: Gradually expand to standard endpoints; perform failure injection for cross-region capacity loss and verify runbook
Post-rollout: Schedule retrospective and update docs with lessons learned
decisions: Adopt three SLO templates (Expedited=99.95%/7d, Standard=99.9%/30d, Best-effort=99.0%/7d) as initial defaults
Use burn-rate thresholds to transition circuit breakers: >4x => Throttling, >10x => Open
Allow controlled borrowing up to 10% of a dependent endpoint's error budget for up to 6 hours when region headroom falls below 0.3 and source endpoint priority is Critical
Require automatic repayment at a minimum rate of 2x normal accrual post-borrow window and a hard repayment deadline of 72 hours
